To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the causal structure of dynamic black holes is not a static Penrose diagram, that the Penrose diagram is a limiting case of the causal structure of a dynamic black hole, and that the causal structure is a dynamic causal structure.

(1) a black hole can be a quantum object, (2) the causal structure of a black hole can have a quantum component, and (3) quantum behaviors of the horizon are not necessarily confined to the event horizon.

(i) the causal structures of dynamic black holes are more complex than those of static black holes, (ii) the causal structures are not necessarily simple even for dynamic black holes with simple space‐times, and (iii) the causal structures can be more complex than expected for a particular space‐time, especially if the space‐time is not static.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the causal structure of the space‐time of a dynamic black hole.
the causal structures of dynamic black holes and their implications for macroscopic quantum gravity.
understanding the macroscopic quantum causal structures of space‐time and how these causal structures co‐generate gravitational effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dynamic black holes have causal structures that are consistent with those of static black holes.
a dynamic black hole is a quantum phenomenon that is not a black hole.

the causal structure of a dynamic black hole is a function of the initial conditions, the initial geometry of the horizon, and the initial energy flux of the matter that is accreting onto the black hole.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the large‐scale causal structure of dynamic black holes is consistent with the causal structures of the static black hole, but with the addition of the causal structures associated with the dynamic behaviors of the black hole.
a black hole is not an isolated, closed system, but is a system that interacts with the surrounding space‐time.
a black hole is a dynamic quantum structure that can be understood by a quantum‐mechanical causal analysis of the space‐time structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the black hole is a coherent quantum system, not a classical one.
the causal structure of a black hole can be understood by examining its Penrose diagram, which is a conformal map of the space‐time into a compactified Minkowski space.

the causal structure of a dynamic black hole is a time‐dependent structure that evolves from a singularity, through the formation of a black hole, through its growth, and then its eventual evaporation.
